thread:
Liang: Quick sync — we need to lock down span naming + semantic attrs for LLM inference requests (model, tokens, cache, routing, exporters, retention). I sketched a proposal below, want short takes on cardinality, PII, and exporter routing.

Maya: please drop the proposal here, concise is fine.

Liang: Proposal sketch: keep span name generic and low-cardinality, put variable things in attributes. Example patterns: 
```
span.name = "inference.request"  # avoid embedding full model identifier in name to reduce index explosion
service.name = "redwood-inference"
```
Core attributes (suggested): 
- `model.name` (e.g. `llama2`) 
- `model.version` (e.g. `13b`) 
- `model.variant` (e.g. `q4_0`, `fp16`) 
- `model.source` (e.g. `redwood-curated`, `open` ) 
- `routing.policy` (e.g. `latency-first`, `cost-first`) 
- `request.id` (short id for traces)
- `cache.hit` (bool) 
- `cache.type` (`kv`, `prefix`) 
- `tokens.input`, `tokens.output`, `tokens.total` (ints) 
- `response.status` (`ok`/`error`) 
- `error.type` (when applicable) 
- `prompt_hash` (sha256 hex, not the prompt) 
- `llm.telemetry_schema` = `v1`

Key constraints: no raw prompt in attributes or spans; never export prompt text to long-term storage. Use `prompt_hash` for correlation.

Sam: +1 to keeping span.name low-cardinality. Dashboards can filter on `model.*` attrs. Concern: some dashboards can't filter attrs well; do we need a compromise?

Igor: Compromise idea: keep span.name `inference.request` in traces and metrics, but emit a metric label `model_family` derived from `model.name` for the metrics pipeline so dashboards without attribute indexing can still segment by family. That way we avoid high-cardinality names but still get useful aggregation.

Maya: Also: include `cache.hit` and `cache.type`. Add `cache.ttl_s` only if it's small card. For tokens, record integers only. Avoid fine-grained model commit hashes (those explode).

Zachary: Exporter routing / retention plan proposal: 
- All spans -> short-term high-res store (7 days) 
- Errors and latency outliers (p95+) -> copy to long-term export (30-90 days) 
- Sampled successful requests (1%) -> long-term export for capacity planning 
- Never export prompt text; only `prompt_hash` stored long-term 

Also: sensitive info policy: strip user identifiers from spans; use internal `request.id` mapping in a secure store if necessary.

deploy-bot: rollout-notice: telemetry schema v1 -> staging at 2026-04-10T02:00Z; gating: feature-flag `telemetry.v1` enabled for 20% of traffic.

Liang: On cardinality: keep `model.variant` optional; if present, limit allowed enum to curated variants to avoid freeform strings. We should enforce via SDKs and ingestion pipeline.

Sam: Add `llm.sample_reason` attribute to explain why a span was kept (e.g. `error`, `anomaly`, `manual`, `always`). Helps downstream retention rules.

Igor: Small implementation note: use numeric attributes where possible for tokens and cost. But some backends (we use clickhouse/pulsar pipeline) prefer strings — we'll normalize at ingest. Document exact types in the schema PR.

Maya: security note: for on-prem/private customers, consider config to disable `prompt_hash` if customers want zero-correlation telemetry. Make it opt-in.

Liang: I'll draft a formal spec and a tiny SDK patch to enforce keys + enums. Plan: PR -> staging rollout with feature flag -> validate exporters/retention -> prod. I'll include example OTEL semantic attributes and the ingestion mapping.

Maya: 👍

Sam: thanks, good direction.

Liang: I'll post the PR later today with a short migration/rollout checklist. Thanks all!
